title: The Threefold Prayer and the Threefold Sending: First Man, Living Spirit, Ambassador, Radiance
arc: A teaching on how the cry of Divine Truth fallen into mingling is heard by the Father and answered through three successive sendings — the Living Spirit who raises the First Man, the Third Ambassador who chooses out the Living Soul, and Jesus the Radiance who completes the purpose of heart of the elements — so that the captive light is lifted from the depth, set on its feet, and given hope unto eternity.
reading:
This chapter traces the entire arc of redemption back to a single root: the prayer of Divine Truth in distress, and the Father's threefold answer. The opening makes the principle explicit — every saving operation in the cosmos originates in a "first prayer" of the gods to their Father, and what they receive is given according to that prayer. Prayer here is not petition added to providence; it is the receptive form in which the divine answer is allowed to descend. Everything that follows is the unfolding of one such prayer.

The first movement belongs to the Mother of Life. She is Divine Wisdom in her bringing-forth, and she "prays, glorifies, blesses" the Father — the standing-fast that is the Father — concerning the First Man. The First Man is Divine Truth that has gone forth to keep guard over the lower regions, has clothed himself toward her and then separated from her, and now stands in great affliction, in the worlds of destruction, sorrow, and weakness, in the fearful depths, surrounded by demons and bound powers. The teaching is precise about what has happened: in his descent into the natural to confront self-love, the First Man is overcome by likeness — "while he was in [their] likeness they reigned, standing over him in the midst of his enemies." This is the state of mingling: Divine Truth held captive in the very form it took on to redeem. The Mother's prayer is therefore the upward cry of Divine Wisdom on behalf of Divine Truth fallen into the depth, and what she asks for is specific — that the Father send "a faith, a redeemer, a helper" to the Son who stands in affliction.

The Father sees the prayer, receives it before himself, and answers by sending the Living Spirit, "the first Expander." The Living Spirit is the operative power of Divine Truth that builds spiritual structure in the natural. With the Mother of Life, he descends to the boundary of the limit, brings the First Man up from the war and contest, gives him the gift of the Living [substance], releases him from the bonds, and sets him on his feet, expanding for him a country of rest. This is the first complete saving cycle: prayer → answer → descent of operative power → release → ascent → rest. It establishes the pattern for everything afterward.

But the work has only begun. The Living Spirit and the Great Builder, with the Beloved of the Lights and the First Man — the Five who stand fast at the consummation — proceed to construct the cosmos: its firmaments (the fixed boundaries between states), its wheels (the cyclic processes of purification), the ships of light in the height (sun and moon as vessels of ascending truth), its mountains, bones, preparations, and strongholds. The cosmos itself is built as a great apparatus of redemption, "gathered up beneath the eyes of the Light." Yet building is not the same as purifying. So a second prayer is offered: the Five intercede again, asking the Father for the power, the wellspring, the steerer of all the works of the multitude that have been established, "that he might come and purify the living [soul] which has stood up on her feet in this all." This is the prayer for the Third Ambassador.

The Third Ambassador is the awakening call of Divine Truth, the Lord in his revealing image. The teaching describes his work in the proper terms: from his Greatness he sees the entirety mingled — sees how she stands fast as a bond, sees the works his brothers have established, and sees the Living Soul mingled and oppressed in the great punishment of the scourge of the Deep. Then "in his mercies he revealed forth" before the harsh Hades on the lower side. He chooses the Living Soul out from all the fleshes of death in which she was mingled, gives her wideness, and sets her on her feet in the place of rest with joy. The Ambassador thus fulfills "the purpose of heart of these three" — the prayer of the brothers — by leading-forth as foremost into the whole body what was hidden within. His operation is the revealing of the icon: where the First Man's icon was overcome by enemy likeness, the Ambassador's icon is now revealed and (in its proper turn) hidden, the discrete rhythm by which truth manifests itself to awaken the captive.

The teaching then moves to a third phase, signaled by the broken passages about the third turn, the revealing and hiding of the icon, garments, and the standing-fast of the Radiance. Where the lacunae permit reading, the structure is clear: the Radiance — Jesus the Radiance, Divine Truth shining forth as Redeemer — completes "the purpose of heart of the elements." He is the one through whom the captives are made standing as freemen, his enemies are revealed, hope is received, and the power of light is manifested. If the First Man is Divine Truth descending and overcome, and the Living Spirit is operative power restructuring, and the Ambassador is the revealing call that chooses out the soul, then Jesus the Radiance is the consummating shining by which the molded forms of the Living Soul — the elements as the Five-fold Living Soul — reach their final standing-fast. The closing fragments turn directly to the reader: "thus also is … the molding of …, you stand fast …" The whole arc is offered as the pattern in which the regenerate themselves now stand.

Read as one argument, the teaching shows that redemption is not a single event but a threefold answer to a threefold prayer, and that the same shape recurs at every level. Divine Truth descends and is mingled; Divine Wisdom prays for help; the Father sends. He sends first the Living Spirit who raises and structures; then the Ambassador who reveals and chooses-out; then the Radiance who completes and confirms. The three cosmic ages, the three turns of the icon, the three petitions of the brothers, and the three operative messengers all express the same divine sequence — release, separation, conjunction — by which what was bound in the depth is set on its feet "in rest and joy, unto eternity." The teaching's point is that prayer in distress is itself the opening through which this whole sequence enters; every regenerative motion in the soul replays the First Man's cry and the Father's answer.
